filename: Spatiotemporal upscaling of sparse air-sea pCO2 data via physics-informed transfer learning.pdf
title: Spatiotemporal upscaling of sparse air-sea pCO2 data via physics-informed transfer learning
code_availability: The final code to reproduce the results is available on Github https://github.com/sk981102/ocean_co2/.
testbed_rationale: The study produces open, globally gridded 1° × 1° monthly ocean pCO2 data products (1982-2017) and utilizes the standardized Large Ensemble Testbed, making it valuable for training and benchmarking observational gap-filling and ocean carbon flux models.
pain_points: Extreme observational data sparsity in space and time (SOCAT covers only 1-2% of global ocean; severe under-sampling in Southern Ocean, particularly during winter).
Out-of-distribution extrapolation: models trained directly on sparse observations lose physical consistency in unobserved regimes.
High memory and computational requirements limiting temporal window size (restricted to K=6 months, preventing encoding of full annual cycle).
Overfitting during fine-tuning on sparse tracks, which degrades learned physical representations unless layer freezing is carefully tuned.
extraction_notes: The paper focuses on upscaling/gap-filling sparse observational ocean surface pCO2 using a physics-informed transfer learning strategy (pre-training on Earth system model GOBMs and fine-tuning on SOCAT).
